meta.triageRationale: Grounded on the real graph, this is NOT net-new subsystem work — the bugfix module already exists and is fully unit-tested, and the front of the flow is already wired: the 'issue' workflow stage, the triage sizeClass='bugfix' enum + routing + nextCall→workflow:'issue'. insrc_guide's validWorkflows is auto-derived from steering markers. The remaining work is mounting the exported-but-unmounted orchestration seam (advanceBugfixAfterIssue + completeBugfixTracker) on the approve/completion path, and adding a bugfix guide marker section + front-door steering mentions.

api.name: approveWorkflowTarget
api.signature: async function approveWorkflowTarget(input: { repoPath: string; artifactPath?: string; epicHash?: string; overrideReview?: string }): Promise<ApproveWorkflowTargetResult>

parameters.name: input.artifactPath
parameters.purpose: Single artifact to approve (mutually exclusive with epicHash).

parameters.name: input.epicHash
parameters.purpose: Batch-approve every pending artifact under the epic.

parameters.name: input.overrideReview
parameters.purpose: Explicit override reason that lets a review/code-review-blocked artifact through.

returns.meaning: Existing result (approved[], skipped[] with block reasons) EXTENDED with an optional followOn descriptor describing any post-approval seam that fired (e.g. bugfix advance / tracker completion). [c5]

errors.condition: repo not registered / artifact path invalid — unchanged from current behaviour.

preconditions: Artifact exists and is pending; existing review/code-review block gate is evaluated before completion. [c5]
The seam must only be consulted for artifacts that actually completed (were added to approved[]), never for skipped[].
postconditions: If a completed artifact is an approved 'issue' artifact (meta.issueHash present / workflow==='issue'), advanceBugfixAfterIssue was invoked and its outcome recorded in followOn. [c1]
If a completed artifact is a bugfix BUILD reaching completion, completeBugfixTracker was invoked and its outcome recorded in followOn. [c1]
Existing skipped[]/block-verdict semantics are byte-for-byte unchanged for non-bugfix artifacts. [c5]

api.name: advanceBugfixAfterIssue
api.signature: async function advanceBugfixAfterIssue(input: { repoPath: string; issueArtifactPath: string }): Promise<BugfixAdvanceResult>

parameters.name: input.repoPath
parameters.purpose: Repo the bugfix run belongs to.

parameters.name: input.issueArtifactPath
parameters.purpose: The just-approved IssueArtifact path that triggers stamp→admit→nextAfterIssue.

returns.meaning: The composed post-issue advance outcome (existing seam return — consumed as-is, not redesigned). [c1]

errors.condition: Issue artifact missing required bugfix meta — surfaced from the existing seam; the mount catches and records rather than crashing the approve.

preconditions: Called ONLY after the issue artifact has been approved (approvedAt stamped).
The exact parameter shape is read from advance.ts:28 during build — the LLD consumes the existing signature and must not redefine it. [c1]
postconditions: Bugfix chain advanced to its next stage per magnitude (small→build, sized→design→plan→build). [c3]

api.name: completeBugfixTracker
api.signature: async function completeBugfixTracker(input: { repoPath: string; buildArtifactPath: string }): Promise<BugfixTrackerResult>

parameters.name: input.repoPath
parameters.purpose: Repo the bugfix run belongs to.

parameters.name: input.buildArtifactPath
parameters.purpose: The just-completed bugfix BUILD artifact whose approval closes the GH issue.

returns.meaning: Tracker-completion outcome (existing seam return — consumed as-is). [c1]

errors.condition: GH tracker unavailable / issue already closed — surfaced from the existing seam; mount records it in followOn, does not fail the approval.

preconditions: Called ONLY when a bugfix BUILD artifact reached completion (passed the code-review gate, added to approved[]).
Exact parameter shape read from advance.ts:79 during build — consume, do not redefine. [c1]
postconditions: The GH issue for the bugfix run is closed / the tracker is finalized. [c1]

dataModelChanges.details: Add an optional `followOn?` field capturing any post-approval seam that fired: { kind: 'bugfix-advance' | 'bugfix-complete'; artifactPath: string; ok: boolean; note?: string }[]. Additive and optional so every existing caller (daemon workflow.approve, MCP insrc_workflow_approve, gate tests) compiles and behaves identically when no seam fires.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: interface ApproveWorkflowTargetResult { approved: ...; skipped: ...; followOn?: FollowOnOutcome[] }

errorCases.scenario: advanceBugfixAfterIssue rejects (e.g. issue artifact missing required bugfix meta, or stamp/admit fails) after the issue artifact was already approved.
errorCases.detection: The mount wraps the dynamically-imported seam call in try/catch; a rejected promise is caught at the await inside approveWorkflowTarget.
errorCases.response: Record a followOn entry { kind:'bugfix-advance', artifactPath, ok:false, note:<error message> } and continue — do NOT rethrow. approvedAt is already stamped, so the approval itself stands; the failed advance is surfaced, not swallowed.
errorCases.userImpact: The issue is approved but the chain did not advance; the controller sees ok:false in followOn and can re-drive the next stage manually.

errorCases.scenario: completeBugfixTracker rejects (GH CLI unavailable, issue already closed, or network error) at bugfix BUILD completion.
errorCases.detection: try/catch around the dynamically-imported completeBugfixTracker await.
errorCases.response: Record followOn { kind:'bugfix-complete', artifactPath, ok:false, note } and continue; the BUILD completion (approvedAt) is not rolled back.
errorCases.userImpact: BUILD is completed but the GH issue was not auto-closed; controller/user can close it manually. No corruption of the ledger.

errorCases.scenario: Dynamic import of src/workflow/bugfix fails to resolve (module moved/renamed, or build artifact missing).
errorCases.detection: The `await import('../workflow/bugfix/index.js')` (or equivalent) rejection is caught before the seam is invoked.
errorCases.response: Record a followOn ok:false with an import-failure note; approval proceeds unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: Seam silently no-ops for that approval but the failure is visible in followOn; non-bugfix approvals are unaffected.

errorCases.scenario: An 'issue'-workflow artifact reaches approval WITHOUT the meta the seam requires (e.g. meta.issueHash absent).
errorCases.detection: A guard reads the completed artifact's meta before calling the seam; if the bugfix discriminant (workflow==='issue' && meta.issueHash) is not satisfied, the seam is not called.
errorCases.response: Skip the seam for that artifact (no followOn entry, or a followOn note explaining it was not a bugfix issue); approval unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: No spurious advance is triggered for a non-conforming artifact.

edgeCases.input: Batch approval via epicHash where the completed set contains BOTH an 'issue' artifact and an unrelated non-bugfix artifact.
edgeCases.expected: The seam is evaluated per completed artifact: advanceBugfixAfterIssue fires only for the issue artifact; the non-bugfix artifact is untouched. followOn lists exactly the seams that fired.

edgeCases.input: An artifact that was WITHHELD into skipped[] by a review/code-review block verdict (no overrideReview).
edgeCases.expected: The seam is NOT consulted for skipped artifacts — only approved[] entries are eligible. No followOn entry for it.

edgeCases.input: A bugfix BUILD artifact completed only because overrideReview was supplied for a code-review block.
edgeCases.expected: It is in approved[] (completed), so completeBugfixTracker fires normally — completion, however reached, triggers tracker closure.

edgeCases.input: A completely non-bugfix approval (e.g. a normal design.story LLD) — the common case.
edgeCases.expected: No bugfix discriminant matches; no seam import, no seam call, followOn absent/empty; behaviour byte-for-byte identical to today.

edgeCases.input: insrc_guide called after the new bugfix marker is added to steering-block.md.
edgeCases.expected: listWorkflowGuides auto-derives 'bugfix' into validWorkflows with no code change; the existing keys and their order are unchanged; insrc_guide({workflow:'bugfix'}) returns the new section text.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The review/code-review block-verdict gating and skipped[] semantics are unchanged for every non-bugfix artifact: approveWorkflowTarget still withholds blocked completions into skipped[] exactly as before, and the seam never fires for a skipped artifact.
approvedAt is stamped by approveArtifactByJsonPath on completion exactly as today; the seam runs AFTER stamping and never gates or reverts it.

insrc_guide's validWorkflows is derived from steering-block.md marker pairs at runtime; adding a bugfix marker must add exactly one key and not alter the existing enumeration or per-key guidance text.

All bugfix orchestration logic remains inside src/workflow/bugfix/ (advance.ts etc.); the mount only detects completion and calls the existing exported seam — it does not reimplement stamp/admit/nextAfterIssue/tracker.

migration.stateBefore: The bugfix flow is half-wired: triage classifies sizeClass='bugfix' + magnitude and routes to workflow:'issue' (triage/classify.ts:50, mcp/triage-step/phases/classify.ts:51), and the 'issue' stage runs end-to-end (types.ts:81, orchestrator.ts:154/272/385). BUT the orchestration seam advanceBugfixAfterIssue/completeBugfixTracker (advance.ts:28,79, re-exported index.ts:16) has ZERO production callers — approveWorkflowTarget (gates.ts:611) and the daemon workflow.approve handler (daemon/index.ts:610) have no bugfix awareness (grep 'bugfix|issue' in gates.ts = 0 hits). And bugfix appears NOWHERE in steering (steering-block.md, steering-inject.ts, steering-template.md = 0 hits), so insrc_guide does not enumerate it and the front door never routes to it.
migration.stateAfter: approveWorkflowTarget, after stamping approvedAt on a completed artifact, detects a completed bugfix 'issue' artifact and invokes advanceBugfixAfterIssue, and a completed bugfix BUILD and invokes completeBugfixTracker — recording each in an optional followOn field — while leaving skipped[]/block-verdict semantics unchanged for every non-bugfix artifact. steering-block.md carries a bugfix guide marker section (so insrc_guide auto-enumerates 'bugfix') plus bugfix mentions in the routing overview + workflow table, and steering-inject/steering-template reference bugfix, so the controller routes bugs to the tracked bugfix flow reflexively.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional additive `followOn?` field to the ApproveWorkflowTargetResult type. No existing caller reads it, so this is transparent.

In approveWorkflowTarget, after the existing completion/stamp step, add a guarded post-completion pass that (only for artifacts in approved[]) detects the bugfix discriminant from meta and dynamically imports + calls the existing seam, wrapping each call in try/catch and recording followOn. Non-bugfix approvals take an early no-op path.

Add a bugfix guide marker section (<!-- insrc:guide:bugfix:start/end -->) with the full step-by-step procedure to src/prompts/steering-block.md; the enumerator auto-derives it — no code change to guide-sections.ts.

Add bugfix mentions to the steering front-door: routing overview + workflow table in steering-block.md, and steering-inject.ts / steering-template.md, so the controller routes bugs to triage→issue reflexively.

Add/extend tests: gate-mount unit tests (seam fires for completed issue/build, not for skipped/non-bugfix, rejecting-seam → followOn ok:false), a guide-enumeration test (bugfix present, order unchanged), and triage-routing regression assertions. Then rebuild so out/ + copied steering assets refresh.

migration.backwardCompat: The only public-surface change is the ADDITIVE optional followOn field on ApproveWorkflowTargetResult — every existing caller (daemon/index.ts:610, mcp/server.ts:853, gate tests) compiles unchanged and behaves identically when no seam fires (followOn absent/empty). The seam runs only for bugfix artifacts in approved[], so non-bugfix approvals are byte-for-byte identical. No signature of approveWorkflowTarget's inputs changes. Steering additions are content-only and additive (existing guide keys + order preserved).

alternativesConsidered.name: Mount inside gates.ts approveWorkflowTarget (single choke point)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add bugfix awareness directly in approveWorkflowTarget so both the daemon IPC handler and MCP forwards trigger the seam.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend approveWorkflowTarget (gates.ts:611) so that after it stamps approvedAt on an artifact, it inspects the just-approved artifact's meta: if it is an approved 'issue' artifact (meta.issueHash / workflow==='issue'), invoke advanceBugfixAfterIssue; if it is a bugfix BUILD artifact reaching completion (and passing the existing review/code-review block gate), invoke completeBugfixTracker. The existing skipped[]/block-verdict semantics are preserved unchanged — the seam only fires on a genuinely completed approval. Return value gains an optional advance descriptor so callers can relay what happened next.
pros: Single choke point: daemon workflow.approve (index.ts:610) AND MCP insrc_workflow_approve both forward here, so one mount covers every caller.
Keeps the completion contract (review/code-review gating, skipped[]) authoritative in one function — the seam cannot fire on a withheld completion.
Smallest surface for the mount detection logic; reuses the meta already loaded during approval.
cons: gates.ts becomes aware of the bugfix module (a workflow-domain dependency inside the gate layer) — mild layering coupling.
advanceBugfixAfterIssue side effects (stamp→admit→nextAfterIssue, GH issue) now run inside the approve call, lengthening it and mixing pure-gate logic with orchestration.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mount in the daemon workflow.approve handler (orchestration layer)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep gates.ts pure; let the daemon handler post-process the approve result and fire the seam.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Leave approveWorkflowTarget unchanged but enrich its result to report which artifact(s) were actually completed (path + meta). The daemon 'workflow.approve' handler (index.ts:610) then inspects that result and, for a completed 'issue' artifact, calls advanceBugfixAfterIssue; for a completed bugfix BUILD, calls completeBugfixTracker. Orchestration lives at the daemon layer where dynamic imports and IPC side effects already happen.
pros: gates.ts stays a pure approval/gating function with no bugfix dependency — cleaner layering.
Side-effectful orchestration (GH tracker calls) sits at the daemon boundary where other IPC side effects already live.
Easy to unit-test the handler branch in isolation with a faked approveWorkflowTarget result.
cons: MCP insrc_workflow_approve forwards through this same daemon handler, so it IS covered — but any future non-daemon caller of approveWorkflowTarget would silently skip the seam.
Requires widening the approveWorkflowTarget return contract to carry enough meta for the handler to decide, duplicating a little detection logic.
Two places now must agree on what 'a completed bugfix artifact' means.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Keeps gates pure but splits the 'what is a completed bugfix artifact' decision across two places and widens the return contract; weakest on c1/c3 (all-callers, minimal-surface) without a3's reusable-dispatcher upside.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dedicated post-approval dispatcher module consumed by the daemon handler
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Introduce a thin advanceAfterApproval dispatcher that maps a completed artifact to its follow-on seam, called once by the daemon handler.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a small dispatcher (e.g. src/workflow/after-approval.ts) exporting advanceAfterApproval(completed[]) that, per completed artifact, pattern-matches on workflow/stage/meta and calls the right follow-on — today only the bugfix seams (advanceBugfixAfterIssue, completeBugfixTracker), but structured so future workflows can register follow-ons. approveWorkflowTarget returns the completed set; the daemon handler calls the dispatcher once.
pros: Clean separation: gates.ts stays pure, the daemon handler stays thin, and follow-on routing is one testable unit.
Extensible — a natural home if other workflows later need post-approval side effects.
The dispatcher is trivially unit-testable with scripted completed-artifact inputs.
cons: More new surface than the story strictly needs — borders on over-engineering for a single (bugfix) follow-on today (YAGNI risk).
Still depends on approveWorkflowTarget exposing the completed set, so it shares a2's return-contract widening.
One extra module + indirection for reviewers to follow.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cleanest layering and most testable, but adds indirection/new surface for one follow-on and leaves non-handler callers uncovered — loses to a1 on c1 (all-callers) and c3 (minimal-surface). Can be revisited if a second workflow later needs post-approval follow-ons.
